text:
incident-bot: HIGH: sudden spike in anonymous embedding requests from multiple regions, error rate up, latency up :rotating_light:

oncall-sre: paging in. I'm looking at edge metrics now. seen a 6x increase in req/s to /v1/embeddings anon key pool.

eng-runtime: logs show repeated identical payloads from ~10k distinct IPs. likely scraper farm. KV cache hit low, lots of cold starts.

edge-ops: WAF sig 40123 triggered frequently for UA fingerprinting, but botnet is rotating. we can add an aggressive geo cap for regions with highest traffic. propose adding dynamic quota slice for anon embedding route.

product-oncall: customer impact? which customers are degraded?

cs-lead: support queue shows 4 enterprise customers reporting slow / timeouts for other endpoints in eu-west. tickets flagged high.

oncall-sre: ok immediate mitigation plan: 1) enable temporary rate-slice on /v1/embeddings for anonymous API keys to 0.5 r/s per key 2) block UA patterns from sig 40123 for 1 hour 3) turn off batch-async for anon pool if still overloaded. will execute with edge-ops.

eng-runtime: +1 to slice. Also recommend enabling prefix KV cache for common prompt starts to reduce tokens; will flip cache flag.

edge-ops: executing step 1 now: running command:
```
./edgectl quota update --route "/v1/embeddings" --key-type anonymous --rate 0.5 --window 1s
```
response: OK 200.

infra-bot: quota-change recorded by oncall-sre.

security: adding a temporary WAF rule: block requests with UA regex /python-requests|curl|wget/ and min body entropy < 10. applying in shadow first.

oncall-sre: shadow rule looks good, now promoting to block for IP ranges with >50 req/min. applying now.

edge-ops: applied. seeing immediate drop in abusive traffic from flagged IPs. overall ingress rps back down ~65% from peak.

product-oncall: are we seeing any false positives from the block?

cs-lead: picked up one legitimate third-party crawler getting blocked, ticket created, adding to allowlist after verification.

eng-runtime: noticed embeddings cost per request still high due to large batch sizes; temporarily disable client-side async batching for anon traffic to reduce amplification. command:
```
update-config --service embeddings --param allow_async_batching=false --scope anon-pool
```

noncall-sre: done. CPU and mem per instance trending down. latency back to SLO for most customers.

security: recommend follow-up: 1) create targeted rate limits by geo 2) add progressive captcha for high-volume clients (challenge via API gateway) 3) log all blocked requests with full headers for forensics.

edge-ops: rolling a canary SLA adjustment: burst-cap reduction from 10->2 for anon pool to prevent future spikes from exhausting shared capacity.

infra-bot: burst-cap change logged.

oncall-sre: handing off to next oncall in 30m. summary for handoff: we applied anon quota-slice to 0.5 r/s, enabled UA block, disabled async batching for anon pool, blocked high-rate IP ranges; traffic back to ~30% above baseline but stable; CS handling allowlist request; product & security to own longer-term mitigations.

product-oncall: creating a customer communication draft for impacted customers noting transient throttling on anonymous endpoints to protect platform stability. will share shortly.

cs-lead: will notify the affected customers in the queue and escalate if any enterprise impacted beyond acceptable thresholds.

eng-runtime: will open runbook follow-ups: verify KV cache warmup, add anomaly detection alert for repeated identical payloads, and add an eval to measure embedding cost changes from batching toggle.

security: will open an incident ticket for botnet attribution, include pcap/log dump.

oncall-sre: thanks team. if anything regresses ping here. handing to next-oncall-sre in 30m :raised_hands:

infra-bot: oncall assignment changed to next-oncall-sre in 30m.

next-oncall-sre: ack, I have context. will monitor for 2 hours and follow up in postmortem.

incident-bot: INCIDENT MARKED: mitigated -> monitoring. postmortem scheduled.
